LESSON: ENTREPRENEURSHIP

Grade: Grade 10
Subject: BUSINESS STUDIES
Strand: Business and its Environment
Topic 2.4: Entrepreneurship
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Entrepreneurship, part of Business and its Environment in Grade 10 BUSINESS STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How are business opportunities identified? 2. Why is business incubation important?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1.  brainstorm and present on the entrepreneurial skills,  discuss and present on the types of entrepreneurs,  read and analyse case studies on business ideas and opportunities,  share experiences on business ideas and opportunities for business start-ups,  use digital devices or print media to search for information on business incubation and share with peers,  visit a business incubation centre either physically or virtually to explore different activities that take place,  use a resource person who can talk about business incubation,  conduct self-entrepreneurial assessment on personal qualities, 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1.  brainstorm and present on the entrepreneurial skills,  discuss and present on the types of entrepreneurs,  read and analyse case studies on business ideas and opportunities,  share experiences on business ideas and opportunities for business start-ups,  use digital devices or print media to search for information on business incubation and share with peers,  visit a business incubation centre either physically or virtually to explore different activities that take place,  use a resource person who can talk about business incubation,  conduct self-entrepreneurial assessment on personal qualities, 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Entrepreneurship together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
 Critical thinking and Problem solving: The learner develops interpretation and inference skills when reading and analyzing

case studies on business ideas and opportunities.

 Creativity and Imagination: The learner acquires inquisitive skills when determining the suitability of business ideas.

 Learning to Learn: The learner organises own learning and works collaboratively when using digital devices or print media

to search for information on business incubation, and visit a business incubation centre either physically or virtually to

explore different activities that take place.

Values:
 Unity: The learner cooperates with others as they discuss and present on the types of entrepreneurs.

 Respect: The learner shows regard for the input of every member when brainstorming and presenting on the entrepreneurial

skills.

 Love: The learner respects others when sharing experiences on business ideas and opportunities for business start-ups.

 Social justice: The learner exercises equity as they accord privileges without favour when sharing digital devices, print media

or visiting a business incubation centre.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

 Financial literacy: The learner enhances entrepreneurial skills when conducting self-assessment on entrepreneurial

qualities.

 Social cohesion: The learner works and cooperates with members of the team when discussing and presenting on the types

of entrepreneurs.

 Peer education and Mentorship: The learner enhances interpersonal relationships when brainstorming and presenting on

the entrepreneurial skills.

 Internet safety and Security: Responsible online behaviour is enhanced as the learner uses digital media to search for

information on business incubation and share with peers.
